result.summary: Configure Guix release builds for Linux x86_64 and aarch64 to produce non-GUI binaries (bitcoind and CLI tools) as static position-independent executables (-static-pie) using glibc 2.44. Apply patches to glibc to eliminate non-deterministic store paths and avoid dlopen in NSS modules, while mapping store paths with compiler prefix flags. Update symbol and security checks to validate static ELFs without dynamic interpreters.
result.problem: Linux release binaries dynamically link against glibc, preventing them from running on non-glibc distributions such as Alpine or on systems with glibc versions older than the build toolchain's. Dynamic linking also complicates security hardening features such as pointer authentication on aarch64 (#19075).
evidence: PR description: 'Using glibc for static builds, would be less of a leap compared to switching to musl libc (POC in #23203).'

Release notes: 'Release binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux (except for bitcoin-qt) are now compiled with -static-pie, making them more portable. They can now be run on non-glibc based systems, as well as on systems than ship with older glibcs, than were previously supported.'
result.scope_notes: Modifies Guix package definitions for glibc, adds glibc patches for deterministic store paths and NSS static linking, and modifies post-build ELF validation scripts.
result.changed_since_previous: Added a Guix helper generating `-ffile-prefix-map` flags to remap `/gnu/store` directories to `/usr` in CFLAGS and CPPFLAGS when compiling glibc.
result.card: Configures Guix to build official Linux x86_64 and aarch64 release binaries (excluding bitcoin-qt) as static position-independent executables (-static-pie) using glibc 2.44. This allows bitcoind and command-line utilities to run on musl-based distributions like Alpine Linux and on older Linux installations without dynamic linker dependencies, and enables aarch64 pointer authentication (#19075). A known trade-off is that dynamic NSS modules (such as mDNS, LDAP, or SSSD) will no longer function for name resolution in bitcoind. Post-build symbol and security checks are adjusted to inspect static ELF executables.

risk.why: Alters the toolchain and binary linkage of Linux release executables, which could cause subtle runtime breakage or regressions in host name resolution.
